_what_this_file_is: Every AcroForm leaf name on Form 433-A(OIC) that is KNOWN TO DESCRIBE SOMETHING OTHER THAN THE CELL IT NAMES, with the printed evidence that settled each one. It is a registry, not a binding: nothing here is read by any fill engine and no map key is resolved through it. validate-map.mjs asserts it against the PDF and against 433aoi.map.json, so a lie declared here cannot quietly stop being true.
_why_a_file_and_not_twelve_paragraphs: Two reasons, and neither is tidiness. (1) 433-B(OIC) is drawn from the same template lineage as this form and will very likely inherit both the leaf names and the lies; a machine-checked list can be diffed against the next form's field enumeration, and prose spread across slice reports cannot. (2) A preparer or a later author reading 433aoi.map.json in a year will see a map key whose name disagrees with the field it points at, and the honest first assumption is that the MAP is wrong. This file is the standing answer: the map is right, the leaf name is wrong, and here is the printed page that says so.
_the_standing_rule_this_file_exists_to_d: A binding on this form comes from the printed caption and the widget rectangle. A leaf name is never evidence - not when it disagrees with the page, and not when it agrees, because on this form a name that happens to be right is a coincidence. The controls at the bottom of this file are the proof: nine cells across four pages sit under an identical printed 'X .8 = $', eight are named Times_8 / times_8, and one is named Times_7. The eight that agree do not make the name a witness; they make the one that disagrees invisible to anyone who trusts names.
_counting: TWENTY-TWO ACTIVE LIES. The running count in 433aoi.map.json._notes reached 'eleven' by slice 3 and that number double-counted one entry: _notes[2] item (3), topmostSubform[0].F433-A-OIC_Page6[0].Interest_Dividends[1], is described in its own sentence as 'the only true one of the four' and is NOT a lie. Through slice 3 the honest count is TEN. Slice 4 added two, both on page 4 and both the page-4 twins of page-2 lies already recorded, taking it to twelve; slice 5 added L13 and L14, taking it to fourteen; slice 7 added eight in one go - L15 through L22 - taking it to twenty-two, of which six are the page-7 litigation block alone. THIS SENTENCE ITSELF THEN DRIFTED, and that is the finding worth keeping: it read TWELVE for a whole slice after the list underneath it held fourteen, in the one file in this repo written specifically to explain why a retyped count cannot be trusted. It is now derived by adapters/pdf/count-sweep.mjs from entries[] by kind, in the same place _tally is, so the prose and the tally cannot disagree with the list or with each other. The verified-true entries are kept here as CONTROLS rather than deleted: a registry that lists only the failures cannot tell a reader whether a name family is unreliable or whether nobody checked it.
_what_is_machine_checked_and_what_is_not: CHECKED by validate-map.mjs: every `path` exists verbatim in 433aoi.fields.json (or, for a `container` entry, at least one enumerated field is a descendant of it); every non-null `bound_to` resolves through 433aoi.map.json to exactly this `path`; every entry declares a `kind` the validator knows; and no two entries claim the same path. NOT CHECKED, and deliberately: `printed_line`, `printed_line_at`, `printed_marker_at` and `rect` are transcriptions of the drawn page. Asserting those in code would mean re-deriving from the PDF the very reading the entry records, which is circular. They are quoted verbatim so a human can re-measure them with adapters/pdf/align-block.mjs and adapters/pdf/line-markers.mjs, which is how each one was taken.

_kinds.lie: The leaf name describes something other than the cell. Counted in the active total.
_kinds.container: A SUBFORM, not a field. The lie is the subform name; its children are told apart only by it. Counted in the active total. `path` is a prefix, not an enumerated field.
_kinds.inherited: The leaf name is defensible on its own and misleads only because of the container it sits in. NOT counted in the active total; recorded so the count cannot be inflated by re-listing a container lie once per child.
_kinds.control: VERIFIED TRUE against the printed page. Not a lie. Recorded so the registry states what it checked and did not find, and so the running count cannot absorb one by accident.
_kinds.page_imprecise: The leaf name UNDERSTATES the cell, and the printed page understates it the same way. Not a lie - the name echoes the page rather than contradicting it - and not a control, because it is not verified true either. NOT counted in the active total. Recorded so the finding survives into the forms that inherit this block (433-B(OIC)) instead of being re-litigated from nothing.

_tally._the_three_counts: THE REGISTRY REPORTS THREE COUNTS AND NOT ONE. active_lies is names that disagree with the page. controls_verified_true is names that were checked and AGREE - kept so a reader can tell an unreliable name family from an unchecked one, and so the lie total cannot absorb one by accident. page_imprecise is names that understate a cell the page also understates - neither wrong nor verified right. A single number could not carry any of that, and a single number is how the count reached eleven when the honest figure was ten.
_tally._how_this_is_derived: COMPUTED FROM entries[] BY LENGTH, not retyped. The eleven-versus-twelve error entered because the total was a sentence someone re-typed each cycle while the list underneath it changed.
_tally._slice_7: Slice 7 added eight lies and three controls and closed L14 by binding it. THE PAGE-7 LITIGATION BLOCK IS THE WORST NAME FAMILY ON THIS FORM: six of its seven cells are named for something else — four Name_Creditor indices holding a venue, a representative, a date and a subject; a Date_Final_Payment holding a docket number; and a Gross_Receipts holding an amount in dispute. Not one of the six could be bound by name. Two of the eight new entries (L21, L22) are a new SHAPE of lie — an index implying a printed position the page does not give it — and whether the active-lie total should count that shape is carried open as C-19 and C-20.
_tally._what_unbound_means_now: ENTRIES WHOSE `bound_to` IS NULL, AND NOTHING MORE. The key was `unbound_because_the_page_is_unauthored` through slice 6, when the only such entry was L14 — recorded against page 7 while page 7 was unauthored, so the name and the filter agreed by coincidence. Slice 7 bound L14 and added C08, a control on Date_Signed_1[0] that is unbound because the map declares it NEVER AUTO-FILLED, which is not an unauthored page. A key naming a reason its own filter does not test is the same defect as a count nobody derives, one level up, so the key was renamed rather than the entry excused. Each unbound entry states its own reason in `not_bound_because`.
